en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga) within the Section on Female Celestial Mansions (Itthivimāna)
1. The First Story of the Golden Throne Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
“Your magnificent throne is made of gold;”
He goes with the speed of thought wherever he desires;
adorned, wearing garlands, and well-robed,
he shines like lightning upon a mountain peak.
By what means is your complexion so radiant,
by what means do you prosper here,
and from where do your riches arise?
"Whatever things are dear to the mind—
O goddess of great power, I ask you:
what merit did you perform when you were a human being?"
“By what means have you come to possess such blazing majesty,
and why does your radiance illuminate all directions?
That deity, being delighted, [replied:]
Questioned by Moggallāna,
she answered the question asked,
[explaining] the fruit of that karma.
“Among humans, having become a human myself,
I gave a seat to those who had approached me;
I paid homage and performed the añjali-gesture.
And according to my power, I gave gifts.
Because of that, such is my complexion;
because of that, it is perfected here for me.
And riches arise for me,
whatever is pleasing to the mind.
I declare this to you, O monk of great power.
"While I was a human being, I performed meritorious deeds;
therefore, my majestic power blazes forth in this way,
and my complexion illuminates all directions."
The First Throne Mansion is finished.
